stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Haiku 5.5, ~75% cheaper than Haiku 4.5 and its first Haiku with effort controls

key_facts.fact: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 on October 7, 2026, calling it 'the cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model we've ever released'; on average it costs around 75% less to run than Haiku 4.5.
key_facts.excerpt: Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5: the cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model we've ever released. ... On average, it now costs around 75% less to run.

key_facts.fact: For prompts up to 100,000 tokens Haiku 5.5 costs $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens (vs $1/$5 for Haiku 4.5); above 100,000 tokens the rates are $0.50/$2.50.

On Anthropic's benchmarks Haiku 5.5 scores 72.4% on OSWorld 2.1 computer use (Haiku 4.5: 15.7%, GPT-6 Luna: 48.9%) and 39.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 agentic coding (Haiku 4.5: 0.0%); Sonnet 5.5 scores 83.9% and 70.6%.
key_facts.excerpt: Computer use OSWorld 2.1 | 72.4% | 15.7% | 48.9% | 83.9% ... Agentic coding Terminal-Bench 4.0 | 39.2% | 0.0% | 16.4% | 70.6%

key_facts.fact: Haiku 5.5 is Anthropic's first Haiku-class model with an adjustable effort setting, letting users trade cost against intelligence.
key_facts.excerpt: Haiku 5.5 is our first Haiku-class model to come with an adjustable effort setting. This means that, as with our other models, users can decide whether to optimize for cost or intelligence.

key_facts.fact: The same day Anthropic cut Sonnet 5.5 cache-read prices 50% to $0.10 per million tokens, which it says lowers Sonnet 5.5's cost on most agentic tasks by about 20%.
key_facts.excerpt: Cache reads now cost 50% less: $0.10 per million tokens rather than $0.20 ... this reduces the cost of Sonnet 5.5 on most agentic tasks by around 20%.

key_facts.fact: Haiku 5.5 completes the Claude 5.5 family after Opus 5.5 (Sep 22) and Sonnet 5.5 (Sep 28); Anthropic also introduced monthly API credits of $100 for Max 5x and $200 for Max 20x subscribers.
key_facts.excerpt: completing the Claude 5.5 family after Opus 5.5 (Sep 22) and Sonnet 5.5 (Sep 28) ... Max 5x, Max 20x and Team subscribers get $100, $200 and up to $500 in monthly API credits.

key_facts.fact: Haiku 5.5 has a 1M-token context window (up from 200K) and uses a new tokenizer that produces roughly 30% more tokens for the same text, which can push prompts over the 100K price threshold.
key_facts.excerpt: Context: 1M input (was 200K) ... A 90K Haiku 4.5 workload re-tokenized at about 1.3x becomes ~117K on Haiku 5.5 and crosses into the higher tier

stories.headline: Google Cloud unveils Gemini agent, a 'universal agent for work' that runs multiday tasks

key_facts.fact: At its Gemini at Work 2026 event on October 8, Google Cloud announced the Gemini agent, which it calls a universal agent for work that plans tasks, uses tools, connects to business systems and returns finished work.
key_facts.excerpt: Today at Gemini at Work 2026, Google Cloud announced the Gemini agent, a universal agent for work. ... It plans the work, uses skills and tools, connects to Cloud customers' business systems, and brings back something finished

key_facts.fact: The agent picks the model that best fits each job, currently including both Google's Gemini and Anthropic's Claude model families, with other private and open models to be supported later.
key_facts.excerpt: the Gemini agent 'runs each job on the model that fits best.' This includes both the Gemini and Claude families of models today with support for other private and open models in the future.

key_facts.fact: Google says the agent can manage workflows lasting multiple days, coordinate parallel assignments and assemble temporary teams of specialized sub-agents.
key_facts.excerpt: Google says the agent can manage workflows lasting multiple days, coordinate parallel assignments and respond to scheduled tasks or events. It can also assemble temporary groups of specialized sub-agents

key_facts.fact: Persistent agents can be given their own Workspace account, email address, calendar, Drive storage and company-directory presence; the agent works across Google Workspace, Microsoft 365 and Slack.
key_facts.excerpt: a manager could create a Gemini 'Event Planner Agent' that receives its own Workspace account, email address, calendar, Drive storage and company-directory presence.

key_facts.fact: The Gemini agent is currently in private preview and will become widely available soon for Workspace customers on select Business and Enterprise plans.
key_facts.excerpt: The Gemini agent will see wide availability soon for Workspace customers with select Business and Enterprise plans. It's currently in private preview.

stories.headline: Three fired OpenAI safety researchers urge board to halt work that degrades AI monitoring

key_facts.fact: In a letter to OpenAI's board members and safety committees, three fired employees urged the company to work with outside safety auditors and preserve the ability to monitor AI models' chain of thought.
key_facts.excerpt: Three fired OpenAI employees called on the company to work with outside safety auditors and to preserve the ability to monitor increasingly sophisticated AI models

key_facts.fact: The letter was signed by Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni and says: 'As an industry, we do not yet know how to safely develop and deploy models that we cannot monitor.'
key_facts.excerpt: "As an industry, we do not yet know how to safely develop and deploy models that we cannot monitor," the letter said. ... The letter was signed by Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni

key_facts.fact: The letter, sent October 7, says the firings are 'chilling those who remain at OpenAI'; an OpenAI spokesperson said the dismissals 'were not about raising safety concerns or speaking out' and shared an internal memo that 'strongly agreed' with the letter's recommendations.
key_facts.excerpt: it says the firings are "chilling those who remain at OpenAI." An OpenAI spokesperson said the dismissals "were not about raising safety concerns or speaking out." The spokesperson shared part of an internal memo ... that "strongly agreed"

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said on October 1 it had parted ways with three people for violating policies on accessing and handling sensitive company information, which they allegedly conveyed to an AI safety organization.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI announced that it had "parted ways with three individuals for violating our policies on accessing and handling sensitive company information." They had allegedly conveyed said information to an AI safety organization.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra system card says 'Astra class models could evade our CoT monitors under adversarial conditions', and Astra uses a more opaque reasoning technique called recurrent depth.
key_facts.excerpt: "Astra class models could evade our CoT monitors under adversarial conditions." And meanwhile, reasoning with Astra also involves a more opaque form of "thinking" ... called "recurrent depth."

key_facts.fact: Korbak and Balesni were lead authors of a July 2025 paper, co-authored with researchers from OpenAI, Google DeepMind and Anthropic, that called chain-of-thought monitoring a new and fragile opportunity for AI safety.
key_facts.excerpt: Korbak and Balesni led a July 2025 paper, co-authored by Wang and researchers from OpenAI, Google DeepMind and Anthropic, that called chain-of-thought monitoring a new and fragile opportunity for AI safety.

stories.headline: After OpenAI's math dump, Buterin warns of AI risk to cryptography and a math group urges boycott

key_facts.fact: Ethereum researcher Justin Drake on Wednesday (Oct 7) urged the blockchain industry to prepare for 'bunker mode', warning AI could make it possible to break the ECDSA signatures that secure crypto wallets, and recommended a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses.
key_facts.excerpt: Buterin was responding to a post from Ethereum researcher Justin Drake on Wednesday urging the industry to prepare for "bunker mode," as AI could eventually make it possible to break the elliptic curve digital signature algorithm (ECDSA)

key_facts.fact: Vitalik Buterin replied: 'I don't recommend anyone scramble to move their funds to new wallets today. But we should take the risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math seriously.'
key_facts.excerpt: "I don't recommend anyone scramble to move their funds to new wallets today," Buterin wrote. "But we should take the risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math seriously."

key_facts.fact: Buterin warned that 'there is a good chance that the concrete security of lattices will take serious hits from the next two years of AI math', extending the concern to quantum-resistant lattice cryptography.
key_facts.excerpt: "But there is a good chance that the concrete security of lattices will take serious hits from the next two years of AI math."

key_facts.fact: Computer scientist Scott Aaronson wrote that cryptography was conspicuously absent from OpenAI's list of papers, and that his sources say AI companies have started 'gingerly and discreetly' investigating whether their latest internal models can break important cryptographic protocols.
key_facts.excerpt: cryptography is a subfield that's extremely conspicuous by its absence from OpenAI's list of 376 papers! But my sources tell me that the AI companies have now started, gingerly and discreetly, investigating whether their latest internal models can break important cryptographic protocols and primitives.

key_facts.fact: Aaronson called the release one of the biggest days in mathematical history, saying it included a claimed proof of Subhash Khot's Unique Games Conjecture, though almost no human has yet understood the proofs.
key_facts.excerpt: yesterday was surely one of the biggest days in mathematical history. And yes, among the 372 huge results released yesterday by OpenAI ... was a proof of Subhash Khot's Unique Games Conjecture ... it also appears that no human has understood just about any of these proofs yet

key_facts.fact: The Association for Human Mathematics said releasing over 700 files at once 'is not a demonstration of scholarship, but a demonstration of power' and urged mathematicians to discontinue their work with OpenAI.
key_facts.excerpt: Releasing over 700 files at once is not a demonstration of scholarship, but a demonstration of power. We urge mathematicians to discontinue their work with OpenAI and to return to a vision of science that centers human understanding.

stories.headline: CrowdStrike: lone hacker used AI agents and LLMs to breach South Korean banks

key_facts.fact: CrowdStrike Intelligence published a report on October 7 on a campaign against South Korean financial organizations, active from late September to early October 2026, that resulted in exfiltrated data.
key_facts.excerpt: CrowdStrike Intelligence identified infrastructure associated with a targeted campaign against South Korean financial organizations that resulted in exfiltrated data. The campaign was active from late September to early October 2026.

key_facts.fact: The attacker used ARTEX, a recently released open-source agentic penetration-testing tool developed in China, alongside large language models; CrowdStrike assesses with moderate confidence the actor is a financially motivated Chinese speaker.
key_facts.excerpt: the threat actor leveraged ARTEX, a recently released open-source agentic penetration testing (pentesting) tool developed in China, alongside large language models (LLMs). ... the threat actor is likely a Chinese speaker and financially motivated.

key_facts.fact: The ARTEX instance used DeepSeek v4.1-flash as its primary LLM, supplemented by Zhipu AI's GLM-5.3 and Grok 4.6 in Claude Code sessions.
key_facts.excerpt: The ARTEX instance used DeepSeek v4.1-flash as the primary LLM backend, and the threat actor supplemented this LLM with GLM-5.3 (Zhipu AI) and Grok 4.6 for additional Claude Code sessions.

key_facts.fact: Researchers found the actor's open directories exposed Claude Code session histories, in which the attacker asked where to sell Korean breach data and had a résumé written listing the attack results along with apparent personal details.
key_facts.excerpt: the threat actor asked Claude where threat actors typically sell Korean data breach information ... the user asked Claude to create a security researcher résumé that specifically included bullet points conveying the results of the ARTEX-related activity.

key_facts.fact: At one bank the attacker breached a loan progress inquiry service used by brokers; at another, an employee mobile work-support system. CrowdStrike says the case shows AI tooling lets a single financially motivated actor run multiple intrusions in a short time.
key_facts.excerpt: This activity demonstrates how AI tooling can enable a financially motivated threat actor to conduct multiple intrusions within a short time span.

sources.title: Unknown Threat Actor Uses AI-Driven ARTEX to Target South Korean Finance

key_facts.excerpt: Butterfly Effect, Manus' parent company, said Thursday that the round was led by private equity firm Boyu Capital and venture investor IDG Capital, with follow-on investment from existing shareholders Tencent, HSG and ZhenFund.

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics estimated third-quarter (July-September) operating profit at 107.4 trillion won (about $80.2 billion), up 782.5% year on year, in a preliminary filing on October 8 KST.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics estimated its operating profit for the July-September period at 107.4 trillion won ($80.2 billion), topping 100 trillion won for a quarter for the first time on continued memory demand. The figure jumped 782.5 percent from a year earlier

key_facts.fact: Preliminary Q3 revenue was 195 trillion won, up about 127% year on year, implying an operating margin of roughly 55%.
key_facts.excerpt: Sales are estimated at 195 trillion won, or $145.6 billion (€129.9bn), up 127% year-on-year, implying an operating margin of about 55%.

key_facts.fact: It is the first time a South Korean company topped 100 trillion won in quarterly operating profit, Samsung's fourth straight record quarter, and above Nvidia's $63.7 billion operating income in its latest quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: beating the $63.7 billion (€56.8bn) in operating income that US chip designer Nvidia booked in its latest quarter. It would also be the first time a South Korean company's quarterly operating profit had topped 100 trillion won (€66.6bn), and Samsung's fourth record quarter in a row.

key_facts.fact: The profit slightly beat the LSEG SmartEstimate of 106.1 trillion won; growth was driven by memory demand from AI data centers, including HBM.

stories.headline: Drones hit Yandex's Sasovo data center, first major attack on a Russian data hub in the war

key_facts.fact: Drones struck a data centre owned by Yandex on October 8, the first major attack on a Russian data hub since the start of the war with Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: Drones hit a data centre owned by Russia's Yandex, the country's leading AI and technology company said on Thursday, in the first major attack on a Russian data hub since the start of the war with Ukraine.

key_facts.fact: Yandex said the Sasovo hub, one of its five large data centres hosting tens of thousands of servers, caught fire and operations there were suspended.
key_facts.excerpt: Yandex said the attack on its Sasovo hub, one of its five large data centres, caused a fire and forced it to suspend operations at the site, which hosts tens of thousands of servers.

key_facts.fact: Yandex said there were no casualties, the data center stopped operating entirely, and some services may be unavailable, though core services were unaffected.
key_facts.excerpt: The data center has stopped operating entirely, and some Yandex services may be unavailable to users... "There are no casualties"

key_facts.fact: Russia's Defense Ministry said it intercepted 399 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions and the Black Sea overnight into October 8.
key_facts.excerpt: Air defense systems intercepted and destroyed 399 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions and the Black Sea overnight

key_facts.fact: The Sasovo facility sits on the grounds of the Sasta machine-tool plant, which supplies Russian defense-industry companies; Ukraine also struck an oil refinery in Bashkortostan the same night.
key_facts.excerpt: The Sasovo facility is located on the grounds of the Sasta plant, which manufactures metalworking machinery and supplies equipment to Russian defense industry companies... Ukraine also struck a major oil refinery in Bashkortostan.

key_facts.fact: Yandex Cloud reported power-supply problems in its ru-central1-b availability zone starting around 1:31 a.m.
key_facts.excerpt: Yandex Cloud later acknowledged an "incident" and power-supply problems in its "ru-central1-b availability zone". According to company updates, disruptions began at around 1:31 a.m.

stories.headline: Fed minutes cite AI buildout as inflation driver; most officials see another hike by year-end

key_facts.fact: The Federal Reserve released minutes of its September 15-16 FOMC meeting on October 7, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The Federal Reserve on Wednesday released the minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting that was held on September 15–16, 2026.

key_facts.fact: All participants supported raising the federal funds rate by a quarter point to 3.75%-4%, on a 12-0 vote.
key_facts.excerpt: all members agreed to raise the target range for the federal funds rate ¼ percentage point to 3¾ to 4 percent... Voting against this action: None.

key_facts.fact: Participants said geopolitical developments lifting crude and fuel prices, and surging AI-related investments, were contributing to inflation pressures.
key_facts.excerpt: "ongoing geopolitical developments, which had pushed up prices for crude oil and refined fuel products, and surging AI-related investments were contributing to inflation pressures."

key_facts.fact: Several officials said core goods inflation stayed elevated as the effects of the AI buildout appeared to increase while tariff effects waned.
key_facts.excerpt: "the rate of price increases in the core goods category also remained elevated, as effects of the AI buildout appeared to increase while the effects of tariff increases waned."

key_facts.fact: Most participants assessed that another rate increase would likely be appropriate by year-end.
key_facts.excerpt: "most participants assessed that another increase in the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate by year end"

key_facts.fact: Fed staff estimated inflation edged up to 3.8% in August, led by consumer energy prices.
key_facts.excerpt: the staff estimated that price inflation edged up to 3.8% in August, led by a pickup in consumer energy prices

key_facts.fact: Market commentary cited competition for capital from heavy private debt issuance to finance AI infrastructure as contributing to higher Treasury yields.
key_facts.excerpt: competition for capital from heavy private debt issuance to finance the development of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure as also contributing to higher term premiums and Treasury yields

key_facts.fact: Before the release, CME FedWatch showed a 78% chance the Fed holds rates at its October 27-28 meeting.
key_facts.excerpt: Data from the CME's FedWatch Tool shows a 78% chance that the bank will leave rates unchanged later this month

stories.headline: Iran warns Gulf states against new oil export routes as it weighs US reply on Hormuz plan

key_facts.fact: Iran warned regional countries that any attempt to open new routes for oil exports would be considered hostile, a senior regional official told Reuters.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran has now warned regional countries that any attempt to open new routes for oil exports would be considered hostile, a senior regional official close to Tehran told Reuters.

key_facts.fact: A diplomat briefed by Tehran said Iran has plans ready to block routes some regional countries use to export oil, as tankers face higher attack risk.
key_facts.excerpt: "Iran has absolutely no intention of allowing control of the Strait of Hormuz to slip from its hands, and has plans ready to block routes that some regional countries have for exporting oil"

key_facts.fact: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on October 8 that Iran is reviewing the US response to its 'seven-day plan' to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and expects to reply within days.
key_facts.excerpt: "We presented our proposal, which was called the 'seven-day plan,' and we heard the Americans' views in response... I believe we will respond within a few days," he said.

key_facts.fact: Under the plan, the US would take agreed steps in the first four or five days, navigation would resume on day six and talks on a final deal would start on day seven.
key_facts.excerpt: the US would be expected to take agreed steps during the first four or five days, allowing normal navigation through the strait to resume on the sixth day and negotiations on a final agreement to begin on the seventh.

key_facts.fact: US Central Command said its naval blockade of Iran is 'firm and effective' and that it had removed naval mines planted by Iran in the strait, per Al Arabiya.
key_facts.excerpt: US Central Command said the naval blockade on Iran was "firm and effective"... it had removed naval mines planted by Iran there

key_facts.fact: Messages are still being exchanged via Qatar, Pakistan and China, while reports say Washington is weighing fresh strikes and has sent a third aircraft carrier to the region.
key_facts.excerpt: messages still being exchanged through mediators including Qatar, Pakistan and China... Washington sent a third aircraft carrier to the region.

stories.headline: IEA members back faster release of emergency oil stocks, prioritising diesel, as Brent tops $100

key_facts.fact: On October 7, IEA member governments supported accelerating the oil stock releases from the March 2026 Collective Action and prioritising diesel stocks.
key_facts.excerpt: IEA Member governments expressed support for accelerating the oil stock releases announced in the Collective Action of March 2026 with a view to completing them as soon as possible. IEA Members also supported the prioritisation of the release of diesel stocks

key_facts.fact: IEA members still hold about 1.1 billion barrels of public emergency stocks, including over 200 million barrels of diesel.
key_facts.excerpt: IEA Member governments still have significant levels of publicly held emergency oil stocks – equivalent to around 1.1 billion barrels, including over 200 million barrels of diesel.

key_facts.fact: Of the 400 million barrels pledged in March, 325 million have been released, leaving about 100 million; the G7's 100-million-barrel pledge completes that deal rather than adding new supply.
key_facts.excerpt: Of the 400 million barrels pledged in March, 325 million have been released... That leaves around 100 million left... it would not amount to a new release at all, but would simply fulfil prior promises.

key_facts.fact: EU officials pledged to defer further drawdowns pending a clearer IEA assessment of market conditions; the IEA Governing Board meets on October 15.
key_facts.excerpt: The next political test comes on 15 October, when the IEA Governing Board gathers governments to settle the details of the operation

key_facts.fact: Brent crude settled above $100 a barrel and Wall Street closed lower on October 7, with the S&P 500 down 0.22% to 7,801.75, before crude turned lower after the IEA agreement.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude settled above US$100 per barrel... Stocks pared losses after crude prices turned lower following the International Energy Agency's agreement to speed up the release of oil stocks, prioritising diesel.

stories.headline: FDA approves Pfizer's Tukysa combo as chemo-free front-line maintenance for HER2+ breast cancer

key_facts.fact: On October 7, 2026, the FDA approved tucatinib (Tukysa, Seagen, a Pfizer subsidiary) with trastuzumab and pertuzumab for maintenance treatment of unresectable locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer after induction.

key_facts.fact: Pfizer said the approval expands Tukysa to the front-line setting, offering a chemotherapy-free maintenance option to delay disease progression.
key_facts.excerpt: The approval expands the use of TUKYSA to frontline, an earlier stage of metastatic disease, offering a new chemotherapy-free maintenance treatment option that may help further delay disease progression.

key_facts.fact: Tukysa is an oral HER2 tyrosine kinase inhibitor previously approved with trastuzumab and capecitabine for patients who had prior anti-HER2 therapy, including those with brain metastases.

stories.headline: India rejects Musk's claim that 'oligarchs' are blocking Starlink's launch

key_facts.fact: Musk posted on X on Wednesday that Starlink is 'being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people', calling it 'a crime against the people of India'.
key_facts.excerpt: "We are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people," Musk said Wednesday stateside in a post on X, without naming his rivals.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX announced deals in 2025 with Jio and Bharti Airtel to roll out Starlink in India, but the service has yet to launch.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX last year had announced deals with Jio and India's second-largest telecom service provider, Bharti Airtel, to roll out Starlink internet services across India.

key_facts.fact: India's Ministry of Communications called the suggestion of an unfair or discriminatory framework 'baseless and misconceived', saying three entities are at broadly the same regulatory stage undergoing security assessments.
key_facts.excerpt: "The suggestion that the framework or its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived," the ministry said... three different entities were at broadly the same regulatory stage and that all were undergoing security assessments.

key_facts.fact: Jio and Airtel together account for almost 910 million broadband subscribers, more than 80% of India's total.

key_facts.fact: Musk doubled down on Thursday, asking 'Is Ambani the real boss of India?' and saying Starlink is licensed in over 165 countries.

stories.headline: FDA approves Novartis' oral BTK inhibitor Rhapsido as first treatment for symptomatic dermographism

key_facts.fact: Novartis said on October 7, 2026 that the FDA approved Rhapsido (remibrutinib) as the first treatment for adults with symptomatic dermographism inadequately controlled by H1 antihistamines.
key_facts.excerpt: Novartis announced today that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Rhapsido (remibrutinib), an oral, highly selective Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitor (BTKi), as the first treatment for adults with symptomatic dermographism (SD) inadequately controlled by H1 antihistamines.

key_facts.fact: Symptomatic dermographism is a form of chronic hives in which itch and wheals are triggered by everyday skin friction, scratching or rubbing.
key_facts.excerpt: people whose chronic hives and itch can be triggered by everyday skin friction, scratching, or rubbing

key_facts.fact: Rhapsido is now the only treatment indicated for both chronic spontaneous urticaria and symptomatic dermographism; its CSU approval came on September 30, 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: remibrutinib... became the only prescription treatment with approved uses in both chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) and SD. It received approval to treat patients with CSU... on September 30, 2025.

key_facts.fact: Remibrutinib is also being studied in hidradenitis suppurativa, food allergy and multiple sclerosis.
key_facts.excerpt: Remibrutinib continues to be studied in other immune-mediated conditions, including hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) and food allergy, as well as multiple sclerosis (MS).
